skill.name: on-call-handoff-patterns
skill.description: Create structured on-call handoffs with incident status, investigations, recent changes, access checks, and escalation guidance.
skill.summary: Create reliable on-call handoffs for incidents, investigations, recent changes, and escalation continuity.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown fences, documentation links, and ordinary checklist language. One real issue remains: the quick reference includes a destructive Redis FLUSHDB command that can delete data if copied or executed without review. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Destructive cache-clearing command in the quick reference
remediation.suggestion: Replace redis-cli FLUSHDB with a non-executable placeholder, or require explicit approval, target environment checks, and backup confirmation before use.

remediation.issue: Operational command examples may be copied into production terminals
remediation.suggestion: Label all shell examples as examples only, add verification steps, and prefer read-only commands in marketplace-facing documentation.

remediation.issue: Placeholder service links may be confused with real internal endpoints
remediation.suggestion: Mark dashboard, runbook, Slack, and PagerDuty URLs as placeholders unless they are intended references for a specific organization.

content.value_statement: On-call transitions lose context when incidents, investigations, and changes are spread across tools. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce structured handoffs that preserve operational continuity.
actual_capabilities: Creates shift handoff documents with active incidents, investigations, recent changes, known issues, and upcoming events.
Provides templates for full handoffs, async summaries, and mid-incident transfers.
Structures escalation reminders, key contacts, and handoff sync agendas.
Builds pre-shift, daily, and post-shift checklists for on-call engineers.
Captures resource links for dashboards, runbooks, incident channels, and postmortems.
limitations: It does not verify live incidents, dashboard state, alert routing, or access permissions.
It does not integrate directly with Slack, PagerDuty, Grafana, Kubernetes, or databases.
Operational command examples require human review before execution.
Output quality depends on accurate incident details supplied by the user.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Weekly Rotation Handoff
use_cases.description: Turn shift notes into a complete handoff covering active work, risks, changes, resources, and next steps.

use_cases.title: Transfer an Active Incident
use_cases.description: Summarize current status, mitigation actions, known facts, owners, communication state, and escalation paths.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Handoff Practice
use_cases.description: Create reusable templates, sync agendas, and checklists that reduce missed context across rotations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Shift Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner template for a normal on-call rotation change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an on-call handoff for my team. Include active incidents, investigations, recent changes, known issues, upcoming events, resources, and escalation reminders. Ask for any missing details.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize an Ongoing Investigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for unresolved issues that need continuity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these investigation notes into a handoff section. Include status, impact, timeline, leading theories, evidence, next steps, owner, resources, and what the incoming engineer should watch.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Mid-Incident Transfer
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for an incident changing owners during response.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mid-incident handoff from these incident notes. Capture current severity, customer impact, mitigation state, actions already taken, remaining decisions, communication status, and escalation path.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Our Handoff Process
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review prompt for team process design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our current on-call handoff process and propose a stronger pattern. Identify missing context, risky assumptions, checklist gaps, ownership gaps, and a concise standard template.

output_examples.input: A platform team has one API latency investigation, one memory watch item, two deployments, and a database maintenance window tomorrow.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a structured handoff with watch items, impact, next checks, recent changes, maintenance timing, resource links, and escalation contacts.

output_examples.input: A payment incident is improving after mitigation, but ownership must move to the next engineer.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a mid-incident transfer with current severity, mitigation status, known cause, remaining actions, communications, and confirmation tasks.

output_examples.input: A team wants a repeatable rotation checklist for every on-call shift.
output_examples.output: The skill returns pre-shift, daily, post-shift, and sync meeting checklists that help engineers verify access, alerts, documentation, and coverage.

best_practices: Provide current incident facts, owners, timestamps, and next actions before asking for the handoff.
Separate confirmed facts from theories so the incoming engineer can continue the investigation cleanly.
Review any operational commands, links, and escalation contacts before sharing the final handoff.
anti_patterns: Do not use the templates as a substitute for live alert and access verification.
Do not include secrets, customer data, or private credentials in handoff text.
Do not execute example commands without confirming environment, blast radius, and approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create structured on-call handoffs, incident transfers, sync agendas, and on-call checklists.

faq.question: Can it check my live PagerDuty or Slack setup?
faq.answer: No. It can remind you what to verify, but it does not connect to those tools by itself.

faq.question: Is it useful for active incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a mid-incident handoff pattern for transferring status, mitigation work, and escalation context.

faq.question: Does it replace runbooks?
faq.answer: No. It organizes handoff context and links to runbooks, but it does not validate runbook accuracy.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide current incidents, investigations, recent changes, known issues, upcoming events, links, owners, and escalation paths.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
